title: How agents will unlock the $500B promise of AI - Donald Hruska, Retool
talk_summary: Retool pitches agent platforms, arguing agents are simple LLM execution loops but production requires guardrails, evals, security, and cost/runtime observability; build core agents yourself and buy commodity ones. Most content is vendor framing, with few concrete mechanisms beyond iteration caps and per-run observability.

takeaways.technique: Hard iteration cap in agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They put a maximum iteration count in the agent execution loop so the model cannot keep reasoning/tool-calling indefinitely and burn API spend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a number of maximum iterations so our agent can't get stuck in a loop thinking forever burning up our our OpenAI costs

takeaways.what_they_do: They require visibility into token usage, estimated cost, and runtime, with the ability to drill into a specific agent and specific run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: understand token usage, estimated costs, and runtime information for your agent

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat evals as the main safeguard for making non-deterministic agents behave more deterministically before production use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: eval are really an important safeguard here in making your non-deterministic agent as deterministic as you can

takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that production agents need deliberate control over what tools and data each agent can access, alongside audit and permissioning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You have to be conscious of the things that you're giving your agent access to.

takeaways.technique: Build core agents, buy commodity workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend hand-building agents that are core/competitive and using managed platforms for commodity long-tail workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you're working on something that's part of your core product or gives your business its competitive edge, then you probably want to build it yourself.
